title: Raiders (new scenario, Magazine 1)
author: Matt Sprange
forces: Hunting fleet of agreed points (at least half escorts, at most one battleship); raiders up to 50% of the hunters' fleet (at least half escorts, no battleships) plus D6x10 points of orbital defences on top of the 50%.
summary: Raiders have a hidden base on one of two planetoids. The raiders' fleet is split into two numbered groups, one on guard on the table as face-down counters (at least 30cm apart, within 45cm of the sunward edge) and one docked at the base. Counters are activated by a hunting vessel moving within 30cm; the raider may voluntarily activate one counter a turn (two if hunters use special orders). Ten turns.
special_rules: Face-down counters (cruisers and escort squadrons) activated within 30cm
Raider base on one of two planetoids, docked vessels need a Leadership test to leave low orbit
Hunters score bonus VP for ships in low orbit over the raiders' planetoid; raiders score 10% for disengaged ships
xr_dependencies: Scenarios: The Raiders (booklet, a different scenario)

xr_conflicts.effect: Pre-XR magazine text: page and scenario pointers refer to the first Battlefleet Gothic rulebook.

xr_conflicts.source_text: The vessels docked at the planet may not move out of low orbit until they pass a Leadership Test at the beginning of their turn. Note that this is not a Command Check
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Ships in low orbit do not have to move and capital ships do not require a minimum distance before they can turn.
xr_conflicts.effect: XR has a low orbit table; the source docks ships at a planetoid without it. XR s.41 says nothing about a Leadership test to leave.

xr_conflicts.source_text: the hunter receives no victory points for raider ships that disengage. Instead the hunter scores bonus VPs equal to the points value of any of his ships which are in low orbit over the raiders' planetoid at the end of the game
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Each non-crippled capital ship, escort squadron, and defence installation that has disengaged before the end of the game awards the opposing player a number of victory points equal to 10% of that unit/squadron's total points value
xr_conflicts.effect: Overrides the 10% rule for the hunter; the raider keeps 10% for disengaging hunters.

xr_conflicts.topic: Solar flares experimental rules in the same article

xr_conflicts.effect: The booklet already has an Eldar solar flare rule, so the Magazine 1 experimental text is superseded.

title: Corribra: Mission IV, Destroy the Gork's Pay!
author: Matt Sprange
forces: Imperium 250 points of escorts and Captain Leigh (the Thebes may be added). Orks the Gork's Pay (Kill Kroozer), Warlord Gutztoof (two extra re-rolls, Maniac Gunners and Mad Meks).
summary: The Gork's Pay hides in an asteroid field (15cm x 30cm) in the board centre and is not placed at the start. xr_conflicts.xr_text: ships moving through an asteroid field, or coming into base contact with the edge of one, must first pass a leadership test to navigate it successfully. Ships on All Ahead Full special orders must test on 3D6 instead of 2D6.

xr_conflicts.source_text: The Gork's Pay is a Kill Krozer, (page 136 of the rulebook), but Gutztoof grants the ship two extra re-rolls and it has Maniac Gunners and Mad Meks on board.

title: Treasure Fleet
author: Pendrigh Redford
forces: Attackers up to 750 points (at least half escorts). Defenders up to 750 points plus 2D6x10 points of planetary defences (no more than half on fire ships). Eight transports in stationary orbit.
summary: A medium planet with a 20cm gravity well sits in the centre. Eight transports are inactive in the well with the defences; the defender's fleet is split by D6 per unit (1-3 on the board, 4+ the relief force). The attackers capture transports by hit-and-run or boarding and move them; scoring is one point per transport controlled. The defender's relief force arrives from the second Imperial turn on a Leadership test from a random edge.
special_rules: Inactive transports (captured by hit-and-run or boarding, moved only by the attacker)
Relief Force arriving by Leadership test

title: Evacuation
author: Nate Montes
forces: Attackers randomly generated (D3+3 rolls on a D6 table: attack craft counters, escort squadrons of 100/150/200, one cruiser up to 210). Defending convoy up to 200 points of transports (at least 10 ships, no more than three of a type apart from normal transports) plus up to 300 points of defenders.
summary: The convoy is set within 45cm of the long edges, no further than 60cm from the short edge opposite the entry point; the attackers approach. Special rules from the old Convoy scenario apply with modifications: transports individually take Leadership at -1 and roll for orders separately; Q-ships need not be identified. From the second turn the defender rolls D10 on a panic table at the start of each turn. The game ends when the last transport leaves or is destroyed.

title: Cadian Line
author: Noamaan Siddiqi
forces: Up to 1500 points at most. Chaos has 75% of the Imperial player's points; no battleships. The Imperial player spends at least 25% on escorts and 25% on orbital defences.
summary: Imperial forces deploy first on three patrol routes (30cm apart) and a Fortress Zone; escorts patrol fixed routes; cruisers are on standby and arrive on a 5 or 6 each turn once the Chaos fleet is detected. The Chaos ships start on a short edge and must exit the opposite edge. An enemy cruiser or defence platform detects a ship within 20cm, an escort within 15cm; firing detects a ship automatically; special orders add 5cm. Victory by percentage of Chaos ships escaping.

Patrol routes

forces: Imperial up to 2000 points (at most one battlecruiser, one Nova Cannon vessel, one carrier with up to four launch bays; no battleships) with five divisions.
